newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH INSURERS CALL FOR RAPID EMU ENTRY DECISION.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH INSURERS CALL FOR RAPID EMU ENTRY DECISION.

text.p: The Federation of Finnish Insurance Companies on Thursday called for a rapid decision in favour of Finnish membership of Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) from the sceduled 1999 start-up.

"An early decision would remove on Finland's part the risk of speculation and would stabilise interest rates for future EMU conditions," the federation's managing director Arto Ojala said in a statement.
For an investment branch like the insurance business, stable and low interest rates are "vital", Ojala said.
The value of Finnish insurance companies' portfolio investments rose to 237 billion markka by end-1996 from 200 billion markka at end-1995, the federation said.

Pension insurance companies accounted for 17 billion markka of the 37 billion increase in investment portfolio value, while life-insurance companies accounted for growth of 14 billion and non-life insurers' for six billion markka, it said.
Insurers' portfolio investments in money market instruments grew by 33 billion markka in 1996, while the value of their stock investments grew 17 billion markka, it said.
"The prospects for investment opeations are reasonably good, and the market will be broader and more transparent than before," Ojala said.
The single currency area would boost competition and promote cross-border marketing of insurance services by enabling customers to make price comparisons in a common currency, he said.
On the whole, the increase in efficiency brought by EMU would offset the possible disadvantages of the different pace of economic development in different countries, Ojala said.
Finnish insurers' total premium income rose 17 percent in 1996 to 48.6 billion markka, the federation said.
The fastest growth was charted in the premium income of life-insurance companies: up 65 percent to 11.9 billion markka, and exceeding direct non-life premium income for the first time ever, it said.

Premium income from statutory pension insurance grew 10 percent in 1996 on 1995 to 24.8 billion markka, while total premiums from non-life insurance rose 1.5 percent to 12 billion markka, the federation said.
Insurance companies had managed to increase their solvency despite the sharp increase in premium income, it said.
The Finnish insurance business was expected to grow again this year faster than gross domestic product, Ojala said.
